captures: Entity that generated the SBOM. Distinct from the producer of the thing described.
stated_constraint: String. Full names, no acronyms unless official.

captures: Version of the SBOM document itself, per component name/version pair.
stated_constraint: SemVer 2.0.0 (major SHOULD be 1) or RFC 9562 UUID.
note: CDX version is an integer, not SemVer. SPDX 3.0.1 has no SBOM document version at all. Real gap in both.

captures: Which format this SBOM is written in.
Version of that format. Deprecated versions should not be used.
Digital signature of the SBOM author, for integrity and authenticity.
stated_constraint: Algorithm approved by NIST DSS, ISO/IEC 14888-4:2024 or ENISA. No format named.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: signature (JSF, jsf-0.82 schema); also declarations[].signature and citation[].signature
note: THE COMMERCIAL HOOK. CycloneDX has a signature slot; SPDX 3.0.1 does not, so SPDX signing is out of band. Neither spec names a signature format (no Sigstore, DSSE, JWS or in-toto).

captures: Tool the author used to build the SBOM.
Version of that tool. If none, say 'unknown'.
note: Empty is non-conformant. Explicit 'unknown' is conformant. Neither format enforces this.

captures: Lifecycle phase at which the SBOM was made.
stated_constraint: Open list. Examples: before build, build, after build.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: metadata.lifecycles[].phase (design, pre-build, build, post-build, operations, discovery, decommission)
spdx_3_0_1_paths: LifecycleScopeType on relationships (design, build, development, test, runtime, other)
note: Vocabularies do not line up with each other or with the spec's three example values. SPDX scopes relationships, not the document.

captures: When the SBOM data was last changed. Every version gets a new one.
note: RFC 9557 permits suffixes such as [America/Chicago] that RFC 3339 validators reject. Both formats validate as plain date-time, so a strictly conformant timestamp can fail their schemas.

captures: Component X includes Y; or Y is derived from or a descendant of Z.
stated_constraint: Values: includes, included in, plus derived-from and descendant-of semantics.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: dependencies[] (ref, dependsOn, provides); pedigree.ancestors/descendants/variants for derivation
spdx_3_0_1_paths: Relationship: contains, dependsOn, ancestorOf, descendantOf, hasVariant

captures: Human-readable name of the whole AI system.
stated_constraint: Multi-valued: alternate names should be capturable.
note: Neither format allows alternate names on a single component. Spec explicitly asks for multiple entries. Use properties or externalIdentifier as a workaround.

captures: Everything included in the AI system: models, databases, tools.
Entity that creates, defines and identifies the system.
Version of the system. If none, say 'unknown'.
Last update to the system, including model or software updates.
stated_constraint: No RFC constraint stated (unlike SBOM timestamp).
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: No per-component update field. component.releaseNotes.timestamp is the nearest.
note: SPDX is materially better here. CycloneDX has no component-level 'last updated' field.

captures: Data movement between components: endpoints, APIs, agent protocols, external services.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: services[].endpoints[]; services[].data[] with flow (inbound, outbound, bi-directional, unknown) and classification
note: CycloneDX SaaSBOM services model this properly. SPDX 3.0.1 cannot express data flow at all. Biggest single divergence between the two formats.

captures: How data is processed and consumed, including logging and derived metadata.
note: Both weak. No structured notion of 'is user input used for training'.

captures: Input and output types, modality, preprocessing, tokenizer.
note: CycloneDX allows exactly ONE key here (format) because inputOutputMLParameters is additionalProperties:false. Modality lives in the separate cdx:ai-ml property taxonomy, not the schema. This is model-level in CDX, not system-level.

captures: Domain the system is deployed in: healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, real time.
note: SPDX has a purpose-built field. CycloneDX only has model-level use cases.

captures: Human-readable model name.
stated_constraint: Multi-valued: alternate names should be capturable.
note: Same alternate-names gap as System name.

captures: One or more machine-readable identifiers.
stated_constraint: CPE, PURL, UUID, org IDs, commit hashes, OmniBOR, SWHID. Include ALL of them.
note: Both support the named schemes. Hugging Face PURL type (pkg:huggingface/...) is the de facto model identifier.

captures: Model version. If none, say 'unknown'.
Last update to the model, or its production release date.
note: SPDX better.

captures: Who pre-trained, post-trained or fine-tuned the model. Also the security point of contact.
Capabilities, known limitations, and lineage including the predecessor model.
note: LINEAGE IS THE PROBLEM. CycloneDX pedigree is structured but generic. SPDX 3.0.1 has no base-model edge at all, and even 3.1-dev's finetunedOn points at a dataset, not a parent model. 'This was fine-tuned from Llama 3' has no interoperable representation in either format.

captures: Hash of the weights or model file.
Algorithm that produced the hash.
stated_constraint: IANA Hash Function Textual Names. NIST-approved.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: components[].hashes[].alg (closed enum: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256/384/512, SHA3-*, BLAKE2b-*, BLAKE3)
note: NEITHER FORMAT USES IANA NAMES. Both have their own closed enums. A conformance checker has to map IANA names onto each format's vocabulary, and the sets do not fully overlap.

captures: Architecture, parameter count, network type, hyperparameters. Explicitly nestable.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: modelCard.modelParameters.approach.type (enum: supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement-learning, semi-supervised, self-supervised), .task, .architectureFamily, .modelArchitecture; plus cdx:ai-ml:model:parameter:count and :hyperparameter:* taxonomy
note: CycloneDX is richer via the property taxonomy but the taxonomy sits outside the schema. SPDX hyperparameters are untyped strings with no units.

captures: Input and output types, context length, modality, tokenizer.
note: Context length and modality have no schema home in either format. CycloneDX puts modality in the taxonomy (cdx:ai-ml:model:modality); context length only as a hyperparameter property.

captures: All training: pre-training, fine-tuning, continual learning, RLHF, DPO, PPO, GRPO.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: modelCard.modelParameters.approach.type; formulation[].workflows[] for the training run; cdx:ai-ml:model:parameter:tune_method (full, sft, rlhf, adapter, prompt, lora, alora, qlora)
note: CycloneDX formulation can model the actual training run as a workflow. SPDX models it as a Build. Both are possible, neither is conventional, and no two producers will do it the same way.

captures: Licence type, and whether open weight, open architecture, open data or open training.
stated_constraint: Link to licence doc, or the SPDX/CDX licence fields.
spdx_3_0_1_paths: hasDeclaredLicense and hasConcludedLicense relationships (exactly one of each REQUIRED on an AIPackage)
note: OPEN-WEIGHT VOCABULARY IS MISSING EVERYWHERE. Neither format has any way to say open weight vs open architecture vs open data vs open training. This is a named requirement with no representation.

captures: Links to model cards, system cards, papers, documentation.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: components[].externalReferences[] (47-value type enum incl. model-card, documentation, attestation, threat-model, adversary-model, risk-assessment, certification-report, pentest-report)
note: CycloneDX has a dedicated model-card reference type. SPDX external refs are less typed.

captures: Name given by the dataset creator.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: componentData.name; or components[].name with type: data

captures: What the dataset is for: pre-training, fine-tuning, benchmark, evaluation. Public or private.
What is in it and in what shape: financial, medical, image, audio, JSON, XML.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: componentData.type (enum: source-code, configuration, dataset, definition, other); .contents.{attachment,url,properties}
spdx_3_0_1_paths: DatasetPackage.datasetType (14-value enum: audio, categorical, graph, image, noAssertion, numeric, other, sensor, structured, syntactic, text, timeseries, timestamp, video); .datasetSize (bytes)
note: SPDX is clearly better. Its 14-value datasetType is the only real content vocabulary in either format, and it is the ONLY required property in the whole SPDX AI/Dataset surface (minCount 1).

captures: Unique identification of the dataset.
Hash over the dataset file.
stated_constraint: No algorithm field is defined (unlike Models).
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: components[].hashes[] on the wrapping component only
note: TRAP: CycloneDX componentData has NO hash property of its own. You can only hash the wrapping component. Also note the spec itself omits a Dataset hash algorithm element, which is an asymmetry with the Models cluster.

captures: Origin, collection method (web crawl, commercial agreement), post-processing, curation, labelling, creator, synthetic-data method.
note: SPDX has purpose-built fields for collection and preprocessing. CycloneDX has stewardship roles SPDX lacks. Neither has a synthetic-data-method field.

captures: Mean, variance, median, mode, range, skewness across the dataset lifecycle.
note: REAL GAP IN BOTH. No statistical characterisation exists anywhere in either format. Nearest is SPDX datasetNoise (free text) and CycloneDX graphics (base64 images).

captures: Whether it contains PII, freely accessible, copyright-protected, sensitive (financial, medical) or national-security data.
note: SPDX has controlled vocabularies, CycloneDX has none. But NEITHER covers copyright-protected or national-security categories, which the spec names explicitly. SPDX 3.1-dev adds amberStrict.

captures: Software used to create, modify and maintain the dataset. Derivation from another dataset.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: dependencies[] on the data component; formulation[].components[] for the tooling
spdx_3_0_1_paths: Relationship: dependsOn, usesTool, ancestorOf; Build profile for the pipeline
note: Both express it, neither conventionally.

captures: Licence type of the dataset.
spdx_3_0_1_paths: hasDeclaredLicense and hasConcludedLicense (exactly one each REQUIRED on a DatasetPackage)

captures: Firmware, package managers, third-party libraries, frameworks, runtimes, tools needed to run the system.
Link to an existing HBOM covering the hardware the system runs on.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: externalReferences[].type: 'bom' with a BOM-Link URN; components[].type: 'device'
spdx_3_0_1_paths: No Hardware profile in 3.0.1 (arrives in 3.1-dev with runsOn)
note: SPDX 3.0.1 cannot express hardware at all. CycloneDX can link a separate BOM but has no HBOM profile either. Note OMB M-26-05 now makes agencies inventory hardware as well as software, so this gap has a buyer.

captures: General controls (encryption, data minimisation, differential privacy, access control, API auth, anomaly detection) AND AI-specific controls (adversarial robustness training, prompt injection controls, I/O filters, training-data curation).
stated_constraint: Free, may link to a framework.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: properties[] under a private namespace; externalReferences[].type: threat-model / adversary-model / risk-assessment; declarations[] (CDXA) against definitions.standards[]
note: THE BIGGEST GAP ON THIS SHEET. Neither format has ANY field for adversarial robustness, prompt injection resistance, jailbreak resistance, data poisoning, watermarking, guardrails or red-teaming. Zero hits for all of those terms in both schemas. This is unclaimed territory.

captures: Certification schemes, standards or frameworks the model or system complies with.
note: SPDX has a plain field. CycloneDX requires the heavier Attestations construct.

captures: Link to the producer's published security.txt.
note: Neither has a security.txt reference type by name. Nearest fit only.

captures: Link to databases or repositories showing exploitability of known vulnerabilities.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: vulnerabilities[] (CVE, CWE, CVSS ratings, VEX analysis state); externalReferences[].type: vulnerability-assertion
spdx_3_0_1_paths: Security profile: Vulnerability, VulnAssessmentRelationship, VEX relationships, CVSS v2/v3/v4, EPSS, SSVC
note: Both strong, but both are CVE-shaped. Neither can express a model-level attack surface, only vulnerabilities in software dependencies.

captures: Metrics for the security characteristics of the models or the system, such as robustness benchmarks.
cyclonedx_1_7_paths: modelCard.quantitativeAnalysis.performanceMetrics[] (type free text, value is a STRING, optional slice and confidence interval)
note: Untyped in both. No units, no thresholds beyond SPDX metricDecisionThreshold, no security semantics. And in CycloneDX there is NO field linking a metric to the dataset it was measured on.

captures: Uptime, incident resolution time, latency, request throughput, load balancing.
note: REAL GAP IN BOTH. No operational-telemetry concept exists in either format. This is arguably out of scope for a static BOM, and worth saying so.
